correctness.rationale: The map is exactly conjugate under u=-cx/d to u_next=u(1+a/(1+y²)), y_next=y+d(1-u). u increases; finite crossing u>=1 yields y->-infinity and limiting u=U>1, while u<1 forever yields y->+infinity. A small-u ballistic-up orbit and the finite-crossing down set give two nonempty open classes. At a boundary orbit U=1; order-preservation on y>=0 makes the ratio of distinct critical u-orbits strictly above 1, excluding two. On the critical orbit w=1-u and telescoping show w>=C/y and w²y->2a/d; then increments of y^(3/2) give y~(9ad/2)^(1/3)n^(2/3), x=-d/c+(2/(3c))(9ad/2)^(1/3)n^(-1/3)+o(n^(-1/3)). The infinite proof uses monotonicity, summation, and asymptotic comparison, not finite shooting.
